notes: Improved the definition, clarification, negative clarification, positive examples, and exclusion rules for the 'Capacity and Resources' label while leaving other labels mostly as-is.

codes.name: Capacity and Resources
codes.definition: The availability or lack of physical, geographical, spatial, human, or financial resources required to address a specific issue.
codes.clarification: Include tweets mentioning equipment, infrastructure, personnel, funding, or other tangible assets. Exclude tweets discussing abstract concepts or intangible benefits.
codes.negative_clarification: Exclude tweets that mention crime rates, punishment, or immigration policies.

positive_examples.text: @BBCNews The new hospital in London will provide 1000 more beds for refugees.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Capacity and Resources because it discusses the availability of physical resources (hospital beds) to address a specific issue (refugee care).

negative_examples.text: @TheGuardian Britain's immigration policies are too lenient, leading to overcrowding in our prisons.
negative_examples.why: Not annotated with Capacity and Resources because it discusses crime rates and punishment.

codes.name: Crime and Punishment
codes.definition: The violation of laws, rules, or regulations, including the enforcement of these violations and their consequences.

positive_examples.text: @NPRNews A new study finds that immigration policies are leading to an increase in crime rates.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Crime and Punishment because it discusses the violation of laws (crime rates) related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Cultural Identity
codes.definition: The social norms, trends, values, and customs that make up a culture, as they relate to the issue.

positive_examples.text: @TheNewYorker A new article explores how immigration is changing cultural identity in America.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Cultural Identity because it discusses social norms and customs related to immigration.

codes.name: Economic
codes.definition: The costs, benefits, or monetary implications of the issue for an individual, a family, a community, or the economy as a whole.

positive_examples.text: @CNBCNews A new report finds that immigration policies are having a positive impact on the US economy.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Economic because it discusses monetary implications related to immigration policies.

codes.name: External Regulation and Reputation
codes.definition: A country's external relations with other nations, or relations between states or groups: treaties, trade agreements, and how a country is perceived internationally.

positive_examples.text: @BBCNews The UK's reputation abroad has been damaged by its handling of the migrant crisis.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with External Regulation and Reputation because it discusses international relations and perceptions.

codes.name: Fairness and Equality
codes.definition: Equality or inequality in how laws, punishment, rewards, and resources are applied or distributed among individuals or groups; the balance between one group's rights or interests and another's.

positive_examples.text: @TheGuardian Britain's immigration policies are unfair to refugees, leading to inequality in access to resources.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Fairness and Equality because it discusses the unequal distribution of resources related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Health and Safety
codes.definition: Health care access and effectiveness, illness, disease, sanitation, mental health, and physical safety of people, infrastructure, and buildings.

positive_examples.text: @WHO The migrant crisis is putting a strain on healthcare systems worldwide.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Health and Safety because it discusses the impact on physical safety related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Legality, Constitutionality, Jurisdiction
codes.definition: The legal, constitutional, or jurisdictional aspects of the issue: court cases, existing laws, rights and freedoms, and which body or level of government has authority.

positive_examples.text: @SupremeCourt A new ruling on immigration policies raises questions about jurisdiction and constitutionality.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Legality, Constitutionality, Jurisdiction because it discusses court cases related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Morality and Ethics
codes.definition: Any perspective compelled by religious doctrine, duty, honor, righteousness, or another sense of ethics or social responsibility.

positive_examples.text: @TheNewYorker A new article explores the moral implications of immigration policies on refugees.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Morality and Ethics because it discusses the impact on social responsibility related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Policy Prescription and Evaluation
codes.definition: Particular policies proposed for addressing a problem, and whether proposed or existing policies will work or are effective.

positive_examples.text: @NPRNews A new study evaluates the effectiveness of different immigration policies on refugee integration.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Policy Prescription and Evaluation because it discusses proposed policies related to immigration.

codes.name: Political Factors and Implications
codes.definition: The political considerations around the issue: the efforts, stances, and maneuvering of politicians, parties, and advocacy groups, elections, and attempts to sway voters.

positive_examples.text: @BBCNews The migrant crisis is a major issue in the upcoming election, with all parties taking a stance on immigration policies.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Political Factors and Implications because it discusses political considerations related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Public Sentiment
codes.definition: General social attitudes, protests, polling, and demographic information, and the consequences of diverging from public opinion.

positive_examples.text: @TheGuardian A new poll finds that most Americans support stricter immigration policies.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Public Sentiment because it discusses general social attitudes related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Quality of Life
codes.definition: The effects of the issue on people's wealth, mobility, access to resources, happiness, social structures, ease of day-to-day life, and quality of community life.

positive_examples.text: @WHO The migrant crisis is putting a strain on healthcare systems worldwide, affecting quality of life for refugees and host communities alike.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Quality of Life because it discusses the impact on social structures related to immigration policies.

codes.name: Security and Defense
codes.definition: Security, threats to security, and protection of one's person, family, in-group, or nation, including border security and terrorism.

positive_examples.text: @NPRNews The migrant crisis is raising concerns about national security and border control.
positive_examples.why: Annotated with Security and Defense because it discusses threats to security related to immigration policies.
